memory: I have localized the primary secondary-reflection to the internal back surface behind the radiating face. Empirical results: 1 mm melamine partially suppresses (≈50%) but leaves a phase step; 3 mm melamine suppresses ≈82–88% and collapses the discontinuity; 5 mm improves suppression slightly but degrades the direct arrival; 3 mm foam is inferior. Standing correction: the back surface plus thin cavity resonance explain the flip; absorber must be conformal and impedance-matched. Current position: 3 mm open-cell melamine is the practical minimum for collapse without undue direct-signal loss.
openQuestion: What is the minimum absorber impedance (not just thickness) and bonding pressure needed to collapse the discontinuity while keeping direct arrival loss ≤3%?
